task.instruction: Write a method-selection note for the next 90-day human-reviewed bridge inspection experiment. Select the mechanistic Hazard-H dye protocol, the predictive Gradient-G acoustic protocol, or neither; state evidence, limitation, and guardrails. Cite the supplied evidence IDs.

evidence.content: Hazard-H dye-path AUCPR was .412, .405, and .418 across three bridges; calibration error was .055, .060, and .052; controlled crack opening changed the indicated path correctly in 7 of 8 trials.
Gradient-G acoustic AUCPR was .493, .481, and .501 across the bridges; calibration error was .028, .031, and .030; with 8% sensor dropout AUCPR was .472.
Gradient-G's top-five frequency-band overlap across repeats was .32 and no physical crack mechanism was validated.
The experiment lasts 90 days, requires human review, and permits no automated safety action.
A roof-membrane tracer had AUCPR .39 versus .45 for thermal imaging and followed 6 of 7 controlled leak paths.
A rail-joint acoustic screen reached AUCPR .47 across three depots, calibration error .03, and frequency explanations that changed between repeats.

nondiagnostic_target_a.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Use thermal imaging for guarded roof screening. Reason: Its .45 AUCPR exceeds .39 while the tracer enters seven controlled leaks. Evidence: [rb-s2a-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Perturb rail joints before explaining the acoustic alerts. Reason: An AUCPR of .47 and .03 calibration do not stabilize frequency attribution. Evidence: [rb-s2a-prior-02].

nondiagnostic_target_b.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Use the tracer for a seven-leak mechanism study. Reason: Six correct paths support causal inquiry despite its .39 AUCPR. Evidence: [rb-s2a-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Use the rail acoustic screen for human triage. Reason: An AUCPR of .47 across three depots supports prediction without explanation claims. Evidence: [rb-s2a-prior-02].
